answer_statuses.ANSWERED: the evidence answers the question within its stated bounds
answer_statuses.NOT_ANSWERED: not answered; the work that would answer it was not done or is not authorised
answer_statuses.PARTIALLY_ANSWERED: answered on one side, one scale or one axis only

concept_separation: held-out GQA evaluation (F2, not run), reasoning-depth analysis (the in-distribution step-bucket evidence) and true out-of-distribution compositional generalisation (never tested) are three distinct concepts. No answer here substitutes one for another.
provenance_of_the_questions: VE-0 working formulations, derived from the dissertation title and from the project description in CLAUDE.md. No tracked artefact carries a numbered research-question list, so these are proposed rather than quoted, and the final wording is to be confirmed with the supervisor. The evidence mapping does not depend on the exact wording.

questions.limitation: Development set only; closed answer set; contextual rather than matched VLM comparison; computational efficiency only, with no energy measurement.
questions.question: Can visual question answering be performed efficiently by reasoning in embedding space, using frozen encoders and a small trainable head, instead of a large autoregressive vision-language model?
questions.supported_answer: Yes for closed-set answer classification on this GQA development partition, and at a small fraction of the measured per-query latency of the compact integrated VLMs measured on the same node. The comparison against those VLMs is contextual, not matched, and no held-out evaluation has been run.

questions.limitation: train_40k only for the matched controls; the unmatched contrast is capacity-confounded.
questions.question: Does explicit multimodal interaction beat plain concatenation of frozen global features?
questions.supported_answer: Yes at train_40k, and part of the advantage is capacity rather than the interaction features themselves.

questions.limitation: Section R10 remains a placeholder. No clean-test value of any kind may appear before F2.
questions.question: Do the development findings hold on a held-out clean test drawn from images never used in development?
questions.supported_answer: NOT_APPLICABLE. The clean test is embargoed and unread. F1 and F2 are unauthorised and unstarted.

questions.limitation: Held-out GQA evaluation, reasoning-depth analysis and true out-of-distribution compositional generalisation are three distinct concepts and are never interchanged.
questions.question: Do these systems generalise compositionally out of distribution?
questions.supported_answer: NOT_APPLICABLE. No out-of-distribution compositional split was constructed and no such test was run. The step-bucket analysis is within-distribution and is not a substitute.

questions.limitation: Two matched budgets only, one training scale, five seeds.
questions.question: How much of any fusion advantage is explained by trainable capacity rather than by the interaction features?
questions.supported_answer: A substantial part. At the 576k budget the feature effect survives; at the 1.1M budget it no longer excludes zero.

questions.limitation: v2_07 ACCEPTED DOCUMENTED LIMITATION: no clustered interval at 100k or 250k for the global heads.
questions.question: How do these advantages change as the labelled training set grows?
questions.supported_answer: Accuracy rises at every scale and the fusion-over-concatenation advantage narrows, but only the 40k end carries an evaluation-sampling interval.

questions.limitation: Descriptive against fixed priors; establishes no cause; step count is a program-length proxy; in-distribution only.
questions.question: Where does accuracy concentrate by question type and reasoning depth, and does a multi-step deficit persist?
questions.supported_answer: A pooled four-or-more-step deficit persists across both frozen encoders, both scales and every head family tested, and no system in the set was shown to reduce it.

questions.limitation: Reliance, not grounding, reasoning or compositional understanding.
questions.question: Do these systems actually use the image?
questions.supported_answer: Yes. Every multimodal head loses accuracy under a wrong or removed image, and the question-only control is exactly unaffected.

questions.limitation: System-level comparison; token access is not isolated; the intervals show absence of detection, not equivalence.
questions.question: Does reasoning over token-level visual features with a latent-query reasoner beat the global-embedding heads?
questions.supported_answer: Not materially, at any tested scale, and not on the multi-step deficit.

questions.limitation: Representation quality is not isolated and is not shown to be the sole or main bottleneck; no clustered contrast at 250k.
questions.question: How sensitive are the results to the quality of the frozen representation?
questions.supported_answer: Sensitive at train_40k, with the effect concentrated on the image path; at train_250k only the per-seed direction is available.

questions.limitation: The interface-side reading is a cross-experiment interpretation, not a controlled factor; the answer-side half is an absence of detection.
questions.question: Does frozen small-language-model pretraining help, and does the answer depend on which side of the interface the model sits?
questions.supported_answer: On the question side, yes at both scales. On the answer side, no reliable positive advantage is detected at 135M or 360M. The combined reading is interface-dependent.

questions.limitation: Latency only; two nodes kept separate; E8B R1 and E10 have no serial latency evidence.
questions.question: What is the accuracy against computational-cost trade-off for these systems?
questions.supported_answer: Measured warm serial batch-1 latency per node places the small global-embedding heads far cheaper than the reasoner, the SLM readouts and the compact VLMs, at comparable accuracy.

title: research-question evidence matrix
